sentences.text:
Vimla Devi Yadav vs Nitendra Singh on 8 August, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:37314
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Bhagwati Prasad Sharma

On The 8 th Of August, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 2199 of 2009
 Vimla Devi Yadav And Others
 Versus
 Nitendra Singh And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Kapil Patwardhan - Advocate for appellants.

Ms. Amrit Ruprah - Advocate for respondent No. 3/Insurance 
 Order

This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred feeling aggrieved by the award dated 28-02-2009 in MVC No. 13/2008 by Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Panna for enhancement of compensation of Rs. 60,62, 871/-.

2. Necessary facts for disposal of this appeal are that the appellants/claimants filed a claim under Section 166(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 for death of Pannalal Yadav caused due to motor accident on 21- 11-2007 at Gurnor Satna Road by negligent driving of Motor Cycle No. MP-35MA-2458 by respondent No. 1, owned by respondent No. 2 and insured by respondent No.3/IFKO-TOKIO General Insurance Company Limited.

3. Claims Tribunal assessed the age of the deceased Pannalal as 32 years and assessed the income on the basis of unskilled labour as Rs. 15,000/- per annum and after deducting 1/3th towards personal expenses, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:37314 2 MA-2199-2009 applying the multiplier of 17 calculated the total loss of dependency at Rs.1,70,000/-.

The Tribunal also awarded a sum of Rs. 2,000/- for funeral expenses, Rs. 2,500/- for loss of estate, Rs. 2629/- for medical bills for treatment and Rs. 5,000/- for loss of consortium and a total sum of Rs. 1,82,129/- was awarded with 8% interest per annum from the date of application i.e. 09-01-2008.

4. Feeling dissatisfied with the award, this appeal has been preferred for enhancement of Rs. 60,
62,871/- compensation.

5. Heard.

sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel for the respondent No. 3 opposed the appeal submitting that just and fair amount has been awarded in favour of the appellants.
No case for enhancement is made out.

7. Perused the record.
8.

The Tribunal has awarded only Rs. 5,000/- in the head of loss of consortium, it ought to have awarded Rs. 1,20,000/- in the head of loss of consortium considering the claim of wife and two minor children.
Accordingly, Rs. 1,20,000/- is enhanced in the head of loss of consortium.

9. If we consider the arguments of appellants that notional income of the deceased ought to have been assessed at Rs. 2651/- per month for an unskilled labour as per the guidelines issued by the Labour Department of Government of Madhya Pradesh and a further enhancement of 40% for future prospect ought to have been added.

entities.text: Labour Department of Government of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Thus, the future prospect comes to Rs. 3711x12=Rs.
44532/-.
After deducting 1/3rd for personal expenses, amount comes to Rs. 29688/-.
Learned Tribunal has erred in applying the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:37314 3 MA-2199-2009 proper multiplier.
At the age of 32, multiplier of 16 would be applicable

, therefore,
amount comes to Rs. 29688/- x16= Rs. 4,75,008/-.
In the heads of funeral expense Rs.15,000/- is awarded, for loss of estate Rs. 15,000/- and for loss of consortium Rs. 1,20,000/- is awarded.

Thus,
the total compensation comes to Rs. 6,25,008/-.
The learned Tribunal has already awarded compensation of Rs. 1,82,129/-.

Thus, the enhanced amount of compensation comes to Rs.
4,42,879/-.
10.

Accordingly, Rs. 4,42,879/- is enhanced with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of application i.e.
09-01-2018.
Appeal is partly allowed.

(BHAGWATI PRASAD SHARMA) JUDGE PG Vimla Devi Yadav vs Nitendra Singh on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78663594/
